Story: Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy
Retelling: As Jesus came down from the mountain, a man covered with leprosy knelt before him and said, Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean. Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him — the touch itself breaking the rules of separation — and said, I am willing; be clean. At once the leprosy left him. Jesus told him to say nothing to anyone yet, but to show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony. Instead the man spread the news so widely that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly, and crowds came to him from every quarter, while he withdrew to lonely places to pray.
Discussion: The leper asked about willingness before ability, and Jesus answered both with a touch. Cleansing restored him to community, not just to health. Reflect: What shame or condition makes you keep your distance from Jesus? Do you believe he is willing, or only able? Who around you needs a touch that restores them to community?
Significance: The cleansing shows Jesus' authority over ritual uncleanness and his compassion that restores outcasts to worship and community.
